info.name: screen-share signaling
info.description:
Provision and inspect 1:1 screen-sharing sessions.

**Run "Mint a room" first.** It stores `roomId`, `hostUrl` and `viewerUrl` as collection variables, and the other requests use them — so the collection runs top to bottom with nothing to paste by hand.

### Variables

- `baseUrl` — the signaling service. Defaults to the hosted deployment; set it to `http://127.0.0.1:8000` to work against `make up`.
- `roomId`, `hostUrl`, `viewerUrl` — filled in by "Mint a room".

### Two things that surprise people

**A room id is not a reservation.** Nothing is allocated server-side; rooms exist only while peers are connected. An id names a room that does not exist yet, which is why `GET /rooms/{id}` answers `peers: 0` rather than 404, and why nothing stops someone else taking the second seat if the id leaks.

**The first request may take ~50 s.** The hosted service is on a free tier that sleeps after ~15 minutes idle. That is a cold start, not a timeout — the second request is immediate.

Full reference: https://github.com/alexrelintex/screenshare/blob/main/docs/API.md

request.description:
Create a session: returns a room id, links for both roles, and paste-ready embed snippets.

No request body and no authentication. Links are built from the service's `APP_BASE_URL` and `SIGNALING_PUBLIC_URL`; they are never taken from the caller, so this cannot be used to mint links pointing somewhere else.

request.description:
How many peers are connected right now — the query behind a "waiting for customer…" indicator.

Run "Mint a room" first to populate `roomId`. Expect `peers: 0` until someone opens a link; open `viewerUrl` in a browser and run this again to watch it go to 1.

exec: throw new Error("roomId is empty — run 'Mint a room' first.");

request.description:
Deliberately asks about an id nobody has ever joined, to show the endpoint answers **200 with `peers: 0`, not 404**.

Rooms are created by the first peer and destroyed by the last, so a link that has been sent but not yet opened is the normal case — 404 would report the expected path as an error. Absent and empty are the same state here, which also means this cannot tell "never opened" from "call finished".

Liveness, plus how many rooms currently hold at least one peer — the load the process is carrying, not a total ever created.

Used as the container health check and by the hosting platform. Also the cheapest way to wake a sleeping free-tier instance before a demo.
